published_hypotheses: free (non-interacting) real scalar field phi, massless, four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime (FFR abstract, Sec. III.B)
minimally coupled (FFR 1711.09477 Sec. IV.A 'minimally coupled massless scalar'; 1204.3570 energy density Eq. (31) is the minimal rho_S = (1/2)(phidot^2 + d_i phi d_i phi))
state = Minkowski vacuum; all quadratic operators normal ordered with respect to it (FFR p.2), so the vacuum mean is zero
the vacuum is quasifree (Gaussian), which is what makes Wick's theorem hold ('free fields [in the sense that the Wick expansion is valid]', FFR after Eq. (26))
sampling in time only, on an inertial worldline at a fixed spatial point x = x' = 0 (FFR Eqs. (24)-(27), (32)-(33))
positive-frequency i eps prescription t - t' - i eps (boundary value from the lower half plane), FFR Eqs. (24), (25), (A1)

real sampling function f; moments exact for the Lorentzian (Table I, 'These results hold for arbitrary smearing on the time axis' refers to Eqs. (31)-(36)); the smeared normal-ordered square is a priori a symmetric operator whose self-adjoint extensions all share the vacuum moments (FFR p.2)

'Quasifree state' (the hypothesis Wick's theorem needs) is implicit in 'Minkowski vacuum' and is named explicitly for Gaussian states elsewhere in the owner (noise.py:102).

PHASE DROPPED IN THE CANONICAL NAME, NOT IN THE TREE: the canonical entry's name states the identity for general n as '1/(u-i0)^n = (1/(n-1)!) INT w^(n-1) e^{-iwu}'. As a general-n statement that is missing the factor i^n: the correct identity is 1/(u-i0)^n = (i^n/(n-1)!) INT_0^oo w^(n-1) e^{-iwu} dw, so the unphased form holds iff n = 0 mod 4 (computed here, n = 1..8, rederive part (3); FFR's n = 2 Eq. (24) carries the minus sign that i^2 = -1 supplies). The owner uses n = 8 only and says so: noise.py:397-399 'the identity 1/(u-i0)^n = (1/(n-1)!) INT_0^oo w^(n-1) e^{-iwu} dw, since i^n = 1 for n = 8'. A restatement discrepancy in the canonical wording; it binds no use in the tree.

IMPLICIT FINITENESS CONDITION (weakened hypothesis, noise.py:62-63 'For any real sampler f(t)'): formula (V) is a finite number only when INT_0^oo w^7 |fhat|^2 dw < oo, i.e. fhat decaying faster than w^-4; for a box sampler the integral grows like W^6/3 (computed, rederive part (4)) and Var_0 = +oo (rho(f)|0> not normalisable). Read in [0, oo] the equality still holds, and every sampler the tree actually evaluates satisfies the condition: Lorentzian and Gaussian (exponential decay) and Fewster's clamped sampler (fhat ~ F4 (e^{iw}-1)/(iw)^5, integrand ~ w^-3, computed here). Recorded as a named hypothesis the owner leaves implicit; it moves no figure.

i0 PRESCRIPTION HANDLED CORRECTLY: noise.py:388-411 differentiates W at real u > 0 (away from coincidence) and supplies the -i0 through the Fourier identity; squaring (u-i0)^-4 into (u-i0)^-8 is legitimate because both factors are boundary values from the same half-plane -- the same step FFR take in Eqs. The owner itself names the worldline wavefront-set argument for the curved case as 'NAMED, NOT RUN' (noise.py:207-210) and refuses the curved evaluation (noise.py:226); the result audited here is used only in the flat model.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested: did the authors lack data that would change this result? The result has NO empirical input. The Wightman function 1/(4 pi^2 sigma) follows from canonical quantization of the free massless Klein-Gordon field with the positive-frequency vacuum; Wick's theorem is an algebraic identity of quasifree states; the Fourier identity is an exact integral. Every numerical input (kappa, 3/(2 pi^2), 3/(2 pi^4), Table I a_2, K_F) is a mathematical number, re-derived here exactly or to 3e-17 -- no datum exists that could move it. Evidence against the result from later work: none found; 1711.09477 (2017) reproduces the moment-based conclusions by an independent method. Where data could bear, it bears on the MODEL HYPOTHESES, not the theorem: whether the corridor's matter is a free, massless, minimally coupled scalar in flat space (the owner refuses nonminimal coupling, interacting fields and the curved evaluation explicitly, noise.py:220-226), and FFR's own caveat that the 65 moments may not determine the distribution (Stieltjes criterion fails, 1204.3570 Eq. (47)) -- which bears on distribution fits, not on the exact second moment the tree uses. Having more data does not change this conclusion.
grade_evidence: Statement and hypotheses as used match the source (FFR 1204.3570 Eqs. (14)-(16), (24), (25), (32)-(34), Table I, (A1)-(A2)): massless, minimal, free, Minkowski vacuum (quasifree), normal ordering, inertial worldline, time-only real sampler, positive-frequency i eps. Re-derivation (sympy + numeric, independent of noise.py) agrees on every coefficient: D_00, D_ij, <:rho::rho':>_0 = 3/(2 pi^4 u^8), kappa = 1/(3360 pi^4), FFR Table I a_2 = 2, 9/2, 3/2, Lorentzian and Gaussian K, and K_F = 19.80242121506098 to 3e-17. No physical datum enters, so none can move. Two discrepancies recorded, neither a refutation and neither binding a use: (i) the canonical entry's general-n wording of the Fourier identity omits the phase i^n (correct only for n = 0 mod 4); the tree uses n = 8 and states 'since i^n = 1 for n = 8' (noise.py:397-399); (ii) 'any real sampler' (noise.py:63) leaves implicit the finiteness condition fhat = O(w^(-4-delta)); every sampler the tree evaluates meets it.
